data.title: Neon Signs and Atomic Secrets
data.description: Discover how protons, neutrons, and electrons build the universe around us, from the neon in bright city lights to the air we breathe.

challenges.instruction: Build a neutral atom of Neon, the glowing gas used in vibrant store signs. Add 10 protons to the nucleus.
challenges.hint: Neon has an atomic number of 10, meaning it needs 10 protons in its nucleus.
challenges.narration: Amazing! 10 protons creates Neon, the gas that glows brilliantly when electricity passes through it!

challenges.instruction: Arrange the 10 electrons into their correct energy shells. Remember: the first shell holds up to 2, and the second shell holds up to 8.
challenges.hint: Put 2 electrons in the innermost shell, and the remaining 8 in the outer valence shell.
challenges.narration: Fantastic job! Look at that completely full outer valence shell. That is why neon is so stable and unreactive!

challenges.instruction: Let's explore isotopes! Standard neon has 10 neutrons, but Neon-22 has 12 neutrons. Adjust your neutrons to build Neon-22.
challenges.hint: Keep your 10 protons and 10 electrons, but add 2 more neutrons to the nucleus.
challenges.narration: You have built an isotope! Neon-22 has the exact same chemical properties as regular neon, just a heavier mass number due to the extra neutrons.

challenges.instruction: Transform your neon atom into an ion by removing one electron. What happens to the overall charge?
challenges.hint: Leave protons at 10, but take away 1 electron so you have more positive protons than negative electrons.
challenges.narration: You created a positively charged neon ion! When electrons are gained or lost, atoms become ions capable of forming new chemical bonds.

challenges.instruction: Examine this mysterious atom with 6 protons, 6 neutrons, and 6 electrons. What element is it?
challenges.hint: Look at the atomic number, which matches the number of protons. Think about what element is found in pencil lead and all living things.
challenges.narration: Spot on! 6 protons makes Carbon, the foundational building block of all known organic life on Earth.
